questions.q: What does the 'Allow refresh access' authentication option do when publishing a workbook?
options: It lets the server refresh the data connection using credentials the server administrator has configured, without embedding your own credentials in the workbook
It permanently disables all future data refreshes
It embeds your personal login and password directly into the published workbook
It only applies to workbooks published to Tableau Public
questions.explain: 'Allow refresh access' keeps your credentials out of the workbook entirely — the server refreshes using its own admin-configured credentials, which is why it's the safer choice for production content.

questions.q: Why would a team choose to publish a data source separately, rather than embedding it in every workbook that uses it?
options: So multiple workbooks can connect to one governed, reusable copy instead of each workbook drifting out of sync with its own embedded version
Because standalone data sources load faster than embedded ones in every case
Because Tableau requires all data sources to be published separately
Because embedded data sources cannot be refreshed at all
questions.explain: A published data source becomes one shared, governed object that any number of workbooks can connect to — one refresh schedule and one set of calculated fields, instead of several workbooks each holding a slightly different embedded copy.

questions.q: What is a 'project' in the context of publishing to Tableau Server or Cloud?
options: A server-side container used to organize and permission published content, similar to a folder
A single worksheet inside a workbook
A synonym for a workbook itself
A type of calculated field
questions.explain: Projects are how published content gets organized and permissioned on the server or Cloud site — you choose one during the publish step.

questions.q: What does the 'Select Sheets' option during publishing control?
options: Which sheets and dashboards inside the workbook are actually visible to viewers once published
Which fields appear in the Data pane
Which server the workbook publishes to
Whether the workbook uses a live connection or an extract
questions.explain: Select Sheets lets you keep supporting worksheets hidden from the published view while the dashboards that use them remain visible.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend treating 'Embed password' as a personal/practice-only shortcut rather than a production pattern?
options: Because it stores your own credentials directly in the workbook, meaning anyone who can access the connection details effectively has your login
Because embedded passwords expire after 24 hours
Because Tableau Server blocks workbooks that use it
Because it only works with Tableau Public
questions.explain: Embedding a password bakes your personal credentials into the published workbook itself — convenient for quick practice, but a real security exposure in a production environment with multiple viewers.
